newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Italy's Dini says NATO plans need Russian support.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Dini says NATO plans need Russian support.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, on a two-day visit to Moscow, said on Thursday NATO needed to win Russian backing for its plans to expand eastwards.

"From Italy's point of view, the eventual NATO expansion can only take place with the consensus of Russia and not against its will," Dini told a joint news conference with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov.

Asked whether this meant Italy might veto the alliance's expansion plans during a July NATO summit, Dini said: "I am confident that between now and the date of the decision an agreement can be reached (between NATO and Russia)."
Dini held talks with Primakov and Defence Minister Igor Rodionov and had a telephone conversation with President Boris Yeltsin.
In a press statement, Yeltsin's office said the president welcomed Italy's "balanced position" on the issue of NATO's plans to admit several former Warsaw Pact members.
Russia regards NATO expansion as a direct threat to its own security and has waged an increasingly noisy campaign to persuade the alliance to drop its plans.
"Russia has a negative position on the expansion of NATO and will continue to hold this position," Primakov said.

U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright also arrived in Moscow on Thursday with a package of measures designed to overcome Russia's objections to NATO enlargement, including the offer of a joint NATO-Russia military brigade, mainly to be used in peacekeeping.
